Package org.jdesktop.lg3d.apps.webbrowser

Class ReaderExtractor

java.lang.Object
org.jdesktop.lg3d.apps.webbrowser.ReaderExtractor
public final class ReaderExtractor extends Object
Reader mode: a small readability-style extractor plus the clean, ad-free page it renders. EXTRACT_JS runs inside the live page (WebKit) and returns a JSON blob {title, byline, paragraphs[]}; parse(java.lang.String) turns that JSON into a ReaderArticle and renderHtml(org.jdesktop.lg3d.apps.webbrowser.ReaderArticle, java.lang.String) lays it out as a styled, self-contained document.

Only the DOM heuristic itself needs WebKit; the JSON parsing and the HTML rendering (including escaping of every interpolated value) are plain Java and unit-tested headlessly. Uses the Jackson that BrowserStore already pulls in, so no new dependency.

  • Method Details

    • parse

      public static ReaderArticle parse(String json)
      Parses the extractor's JSON result into a ReaderArticle. Any null, blank or malformed input yields an empty article rather than throwing.
      Parameters:
      json - the raw JSON string returned by EXTRACT_JS (may be null)
      Returns:
      the article, never null

    • renderHtml

      public static String renderHtml(ReaderArticle article, String sourceUrl)
      Renders an article as a clean, styled, self-contained HTML page. When the article is empty, a friendly "couldn't extract" page links back to the source. Every interpolated value is escaped via Html.escape(java.lang.String).
      Parameters:
      article - the extracted article (null is treated as empty)
      sourceUrl - the original page URL, for the footer link (may be null)
      Returns:
      the complete HTML page, never null
